title: LMM-IR: Large-Scale Netlist-Aware Multimodal Framework for Static IR-Drop Prediction
problem: Static IR drop analysis is a critical bottleneck in chip design, requiring hours of computation per iteration; iterative refinement for violations exacerbates computational burden, making fast prediction essential.
motivation: Reducing IR drop analysis time directly translates to shorter design cycles; machine learning acceleration of this fundamental task can significantly improve design productivity.
method: Proposes multimodal approach processing SPICE netlists via large-scale netlist transformer (LNT) that represents topology as 3D point clouds for efficient handling of designs with hundreds of thousands to millions of nodes. Encodes netlists (SPICE files) and imagery as latent features fed to unified model for voltage drop prediction. Integrates multimodal data for complementary predictions.
key_novelty: First netlist-aware multimodal ML framework representing circuit topology as 3D point clouds to enable scalable IR drop prediction on large designs.
contributions: Netlist transformer encoding circuit topology as scalable 3D point clouds
Multimodal fusion of netlist and image data for IR prediction
Best F1 score vs. ICCAD 2023 contest winners and prior state-of-the-art

metrics.other: Best F1 score; lowest MAE vs. state-of-the-art

limitations: Evaluation metrics (F1, MAE) reported; practical deployment on real design flows and scalability to post-silicon validation not discussed.
primary_theme: multimodal ML-accelerated IR drop prediction via netlist point clouds
